description:
Find FRESH attack surface: bounty-eligible assets that entered a public bug-bounty program's scope in the
last `days` (HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti, YesWeHack, mirrored daily), the least-hunted surface there is.

Raw scope additions are mostly not new (in one week 57 of 80 were re-added after a removal), so each asset is
checked against its program's own scope history: you get `new_asset` (never in this program's scope before)
and `new_program` (the whole program first appeared in the window: a launch or a first public listing) assets;
re-added, renamed and redacted ones are only counted in `filtered_out`. Additions only: removals are not listed.
Per asset: `in_scope_since`, max severity, the host and its cached `stack` if observe has fingerprinted it
(else a `stack_note` saying to call observe), and for a single GitHub repo its `repo_advisories` (advisories
found under the repo name: a name match, check match.products; recent ones are variant-hunting seeds).
Per program: platform, max bounty, safe harbor, and its HackerOne disclosed-report history (top classes, last
disclosure; null on other platforms, where we hold none).

Facts, not a ranking: you decide what is worth hunting. Hunt only programs you are enrolled in and follow
each program's rules. Then: observe(host) for the stack, program_outcome_prior(program) for what lands there.

Args:
    days: look-back window, 1-90 (default 7).
    platform: hackerone | bugcrowd | intigriti | yeswehack.
    asset_type: url | wildcard | api | source (code repositories) | mobile | other ...
    program: program handle or name, substring match (e.g. "openai", "cloudflare").
    limit: max assets returned (default 50); `count` says how many qualified.
name: new_in_scope
title: What newly entered bug-bounty scope
